The user's question: does a small fit set do almost as well as a large one? Answered here for these lenses by scoring lenses built from the first 8, 16 and 32 of the 64 fit prompts against the 64-prompt lens.

code.wrapper: scripts/exp12_lenses.py (correctness, resumable fit with snapshots, report, choose-n)

fit.recipe: the J++ recipe of jpp_cli (koayon/jpp-lenses README): LRP backward lrp_mode=rlens, target = final block (relative_end_transport_layer -1, block 59), WikiText-103 prompts in load_wikitext_prompts order (>= 600 chars), first 64, truncated to 128 tokens, first 16 positions skipped, 16 Jacobian rows per backward pass, checkpoint every 4 prompts
fit.router: per-layer unit norm + PCA to 64 + k-means K=8 (seed 0) over the source positions of the first 1000 WikiText prompts
fit.experts: merge-experts, min_kept_positions 50 (sparser experts fall back to the layer's pooled Jacobian)
fit.r_lens: the pooled Jacobian of the same 64-prompt LRP sums (merge-experts --pooled-lens-out)
fit.expert_weights: fit-weights on the fit:0 split (20% of the scoreable correctness-filtered items, seed 0), default CondenseConfig; the 64-prompt lens at every source layer, snapshot lenses at the readout layers (weights are fitted per layer)
fit.snapshots: after 8, 16 and 32 prompts the running K=8 sums at the readout layers are turned into experts and a pooled R-lens by the library's ExpertJacobians.from_sums; the snapshot J++ lenses get their own fit:0 expert weights. Snapshots are prefixes of the same prompt stream as the 64-prompt fit.
fit.j_lens: plain gradient fit (lrp_mode none), K=1 router (every position in one cluster), same prompts/settings otherwise, n_J prompts by the rule in data_efficiency.D2, with a snapshot at n_J/2

deviations_from_the_released_recipe: instruct model (gemma-4-31B-it), not the base model
32 of the 59 lens layers (even layers 0-58 plus the readout layers 15 and 45): the fp32 K=8 checkpoint is 0.925 GB per layer and the disk holds ~88 GB
the correctness column for gemma-4-31B-it is graded here with jpp_lens's own grader (one greedy step on the raw prompt), since jpp_lens ships a Qwen column only

evaluation.items: held-out:0 split (the 80% not used for expert weights), scored with jpp_cli evaluate at the readout layers, Readout Filtering on
evaluation.headline: recall@10: per (item, intermediate) the min rank over the 7 readout layers, hit if <= 10, averaged within item, then over an eval's items, then macro over evals (the README metric, pass_at_k_over_layers)
evaluation.macro_evals: MACRO_EVALS (multihop, multilingual, typo, association, poetry) restricted to evals with >= 20 items kept by the correctness filter (ungradeable evals keep every item). Graded during the smoke test: poetry 9/98 passes, so it is expected to drop, as the paper drops it for base Gemma (1/98)
secondary: mean log10 of the min-over-layers rank (continuous; moves before a rank crosses 10)
evaluation.cis: paired bootstrap over items, resampled within eval, 2000 resamples, 95% percentile; CIs cover item sampling only, not the choice of fit prompts
lenses: then jlens_<n_J>p and its n_J/2 snapshot
evaluation.not_llm_judged: every number is an exact-token rank; no LLM judge anywhere

checks.V1_ordering: expected jpp_64p > rlens_64p > logit on headline recall@10. If the jpp_64p - rlens_64p CI includes 0, J++ adds nothing measurable on this model and the R-lens becomes the default reader for Gemma work (it needs no labels).
checks.V2_reference: the paper's 58% (J++, base gemma-4-31B, poetry dropped) is descriptive only: different model and a different correctness filter
checks.V3_fallbacks: number of experts that fell back to the pooled Jacobian at 64 prompts, from the merge stamp; expected few. Many fallbacks mean J++ degenerates toward the R-lens

data_efficiency.D1: headline recall@10 and log10 rank of rlens_{08,16,32}p and jpp_{08,16,32}p against the 64-prompt lens of the same kind, with paired CIs. A count n 'suffices' when its headline recall@10 is within 1.0 point of the 64-prompt lens of its kind.
data_efficiency.D1_prediction: the R-lens (one average per layer) is within 1 point by 16 prompts; J++ needs more than the R-lens at the same count (each expert averages ~1/8 of the positions, and sparse experts fall back), i.e. |jpp_16p - jpp_64p| > |rlens_16p - rlens_64p|
data_efficiency.D2: n_J = the smallest of 8, 16, 32 whose rlens snapshot is within 1.0 point of rlens_64p on headline recall@10, else 64 (exp12_lenses.py choose-n). The R-lens stands in for the J-lens here (both are one average per layer, from different backward rules); jlens_<n_J/2>p vs jlens_<n_J>p is reported as a check on that stand-in, not used to change n_J
caveats: convergence is measured relative to the 64-prompt lens, not to an infinite-data lens
one prompt order: snapshots are nested prefixes, so there is no between-sample variance estimate
recall@10 over min-of-7-layers is coarse; the log10 rank and per-layer recall are reported because a downstream use (per-layer token margins as in exp11) can be more sensitive than the headline

G1_gemma_brew_behaviour.how: one bf16 forward pass per row of exp11's test bank (three columns, h=1..3, 250 per h) and single_test bank (single table), exp11's request rows rendered for the gemma4 family (exp10's renderer, thinking off, 'Answer:' prefilled), google/gemma-4-31B-it via transformers. Answer = argmax over the 10 colour tokens (exp11's rule); colour mass and the full-vocabulary top token reported as checks
G1_gemma_brew_behaviour.metrics: accuracy per format and h; three columns h>=2: share of wrong answers in each exp11 shortcut family (exp11_brew.hypotheses, gold removed) vs the permutation null of exp11_behaviour_pilot (another same-h item's family set, 200 permutations), with a 95% bootstrap CI over wrong items; single table: wrong answers by stirs applied (exp11 q1_single)

G1_gemma_brew_behaviour.gate: an exp11 replication on Gemma is worth its own manifest if (a) three-column h=2 accuracy <= 0.5 with >= 100 wrong answers and (b) one family's share exceeds its permutation null by >= 0.20 with the CI's lower end above the null. (a) without (b): errors are unstructured and exp11's s1-vs-shortcut contrasts do not transfer. Not (a): Gemma composes, nothing to read

rules.A1_primary: Aya helps the multilingual task if jpp_aya_64p - jpp_64p (multilingual recall@10) has its CI above 0 AND is larger than |jpp_64p_b - jpp_64p| on multilingual (the fit-to-fit yardstick; CI only, flagged, if jpp_64p_b is missing)
rules.A2: the same for the R-lens (rlens_aya_64p - rlens_64p against |rlens_64p_b - rlens_64p|). The R-lens has no router, so A2 isolates the Jacobians' fit text from the router's
rules.A3: English cost: macro over the other macro evals (multihop, typo, association), Aya minus WikiText, for J++ and R; 'costs English' if the CI is below 0
rules.A4: overall: macro recall@10, Aya minus WikiText, with CI, for J++ and R
rules.reading: A1 yes and A3 no: prefer mixed multilingual chat text for downstream fits. A1 no: the fit text is not the bottleneck on these tasks (the multilingual gap is the task's, not WikiText's). A3 yes: the fit text matters but trades languages

phase4.predictions: A1: multilingual up by >= 0.03 for J++. A2: similar or smaller. A3: English tasks flat or down by <= 0.03 (typo is at ceiling, so it can only fall). A4: within +-0.02
confounds: two changes at once (languages and chat format): a positive A1 does not say which; a follow-up would split them
Aya is 1/16 English, so an A3 drop may reflect less English rather than chat format
power: 52 multilingual held-out items, so a paired CI half-width near 0.05 is expected; a null rules out only large effects. Mean log10 rank (continuous) is the more sensitive secondary
the router is refit on Aya, so J++ differences mix router and Jacobians; A2 (no router) separates them
fit-to-fit noise is judged against the phase 3 replicate (jpp_64p_b), itself a single draw
